subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw core treat suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` as a built-in cross-channel reply override, and what trigger vocabulary plus `replyToMode` precedence should it use?
rationale: The feature absence is clear, but the requested behavior adds global natural-language parsing that can silently change delivery routing and may introduce public config surface.

options.title: Approve a narrow core directive
options.body: Adopt only unambiguous suffixes, likely excluding bare `thread`, and require stripping from all model-facing and command-facing inbound bodies with defined reply-mode precedence.

options.title: Keep it prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to agent instructions or a plugin/API seam and keep core limited to explicit reply tags plus configured reply modes.

options.title: Require explicit config first
options.body: Allow the behavior only behind a documented default-off config key with schema, docs, and upgrade-safe tests.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Adopt only unambiguous suffixes, likely excluding bare `thread`, and require stripping from all model-facing and command-facing inbound bodies with defined reply-mode precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for reply tags, replyToMode, inbound context finalization, and reply-threading policy is on steipete-authored commits.
